movement_profile.arms_and_hands: Partnered handholds, placing a hand on the partner's hip or bodice, or holding hands while turning in the hall.
movement_profile.footwork: Alternating simple and double steps featuring springing or jumping movements (*pas sauté*) in the Renaissance style, evolving into measured, gliding, and crossing steps in the Baroque French style.
movement_profile.formation_and_space: Couples traveling along the perimeter of the hall, turning, and executing advances and retreats.
movement_profile.hips_and_torso: Stable torso with controlled vertical movement accommodating the step and weight shifts.
movement_profile.levels_and_jumps: Includes low springs and jumps in the Renaissance iteration; grounded, gliding elevation in the Baroque court style.
movement_profile.partnering: Paired dance involving turning together without letting go of the partner, punctuated by brief moments of conversation when instruments pause.
movement_profile.posture: Upright, aristocratic posture with controlled carriage and turned-out feet.

signature_moves.description: A jumping step where the dancer springs on one foot and moves forward on the other.
signature_moves.name: Pas sauté

signature_moves.description: A rhythmic shift where dancers adjust their phrasing across the metric divisions of the music.
signature_moves.name: Hemiola cadence

movement_profile.tempo_feel: Moderate and grave for the French style; lively and flowing for the Italian style.
movement_profile.what_to_avoid: Avoid conflating the brisk, jumping Renaissance courante with the slow, majestic French Baroque courante or ignoring national stylistic differences.

music_profile.meter: Triple metre (typically 3/2 or 6/4 for French; 3/4 or 3/8 for Italian)
music_profile.musical_form: Binary form with two repeated sections
music_profile.rhythm_pattern: Upbeat entry (levée) followed by metric ambiguities and hemiolas across bar lines
music_profile.sound_description: A triple-meter texture beginning on an upbeat, characterized by shifting metrical accents, graceful counterpoint, and an interplay between solemn dignity and buoyant forward momentum.

basic_steps: Simple à gauche: left foot steps to the left, right foot joins.
Simple à droite: right foot steps to the right, left foot joins.
Double à gauche: left foot steps left, right closes, left steps left, right joins with a slight spring or greve.
Double à droite: repeated on the opposite side with reversed footwork.
teaching.formation: Couple dance, moving forward, sideways, or backward around the hall.
teaching.level_notes: Requires coordination of upper body dignity with precise foot placement and springy execution.
teaching.rhythm: Triple meter with an upbeat (levée) and frequent hemiola shifts.
